chief_complaint: intrusive terrifying thoughts of contamination leading to washing hands 50 times daily until skin bleeds
hpi_details: 25F presenting with severe obsessions regarding germs/HIV and compulsive ritualistic handwashing consuming 5 hours daily. A Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS) assessment supports severe OCD; treatment includes Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) and an SSRI titrated as tolerated, often to an OCD-range dose.
ideas: She thinks she picked up dangerous viruses or bodily fluids from public surfaces and that invisible contamination is lingering on her skin.
concerns: She is worried that she will infect her family with a fatal disease and lose her job because she spends hours scrubbing in the restroom.
expectations: She hopes to receive a full viral screening to confirm she is clean and a medication to quiet the terrifying thoughts in her head.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD): contamination obsessions and washing compulsions
core_concepts: OCD involves intrusive, unwanted obsessions and/or compulsions that are time-consuming or cause marked distress or impairment; assess insight and functional impact.
Differentiate obsessions from fixed delusions, generalized worry, illness anxiety, trauma-related symptoms, eating-disorder rituals, and substance- or medication-induced symptoms.

First-line treatment is exposure and response prevention (ERP), with an SSRI when symptoms are moderate to severe; response may require an adequate duration and OCD-range dose under clinical supervision.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: intrusive terrifying thoughts of contamination leading to washing hands 50 times daily until skin bleeds
Key HPI features: severe germ/HIV obsessions and ritualized handwashing for about 5 hours daily, causing skin injury and marked impairment.
Assessment findings: use Y-BOCS to quantify severity; examine hands for dermatitis, fissures, bleeding, or infection and assess mood, psychosis, substance use, and safety.
common_misconceptions: Contamination fears are OCD only when the patient has poor insight.
Reassurance or avoiding triggers is a durable treatment for compulsions.
A routine laboratory panel or imaging test diagnoses OCD.
dangerous_errors: Missing suicidal intent, self-harm, violence risk, inability to care for basic needs, or skin infection; arrange emergency assessment when immediate safety or medical stability is in question.
Treating fixed contamination beliefs, hallucinations, disorganization, delirium, intoxication, or withdrawal as uncomplicated OCD.
Starting or escalating an SSRI without screening for bipolar-spectrum mania, interactions, pregnancy considerations, adverse effects, and early activation or suicidality.
management_principles: Provide or refer for structured ERP; reduce family accommodation and use collaborative, graded exposure planning.
Offer an SSRI when indicated and monitor adherence, activation, sleep, sexual adverse effects, mood switching, and suicidal thinking, especially after initiation or dose changes.
Treat hand dermatitis and infection as needed; reassess severity and functioning with a validated scale.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Escalate urgently for imminent self-harm or harm to others, grave disability, severe skin infection, delirium, intoxication, withdrawal, mania, or psychosis.
Seek specialist care for severe symptoms, poor insight, diagnostic uncertainty, treatment resistance, pregnancy, bipolar disorder, or complex comorbidity.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: intrusive terrifying thoughts of contamination leading to washing hands 50 times daily until skin bleeds

25F presenting with severe obsessions regarding germs/HIV and compulsive ritualistic handwashing consuming 5 hours daily where PHQ/YBOCS confirms severe OCD requiring high-dose SSRI (Fluoxetine 60-80 mg) plus Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) therapy.
reference_soap.objective: Assess vital signs, mental status, Y-BOCS severity, insight, suicidality, psychosis, mania, substance use, and hand skin integrity or infection.
reference_soap.assessment: Obsessive-compulsive disorder, contamination obsessions with washing compulsions, severe; assess insight and exclude psychosis, mood disorder, substance-related causes, and medical complications of washing.
reference_soap.plan: Initiate or refer for ERP. Discuss an SSRI with gradual titration and close monitoring for activation, suicidality, mood switching, interactions, and reproductive considerations. Provide skin care and urgent escalation for safety, psychosis, delirium, mania, or infection.

learning_objectives: Recognize diagnostic features of obsessive-compulsive disorder, including obsessions, compulsions, insight, distress, and impairment
Formulate prioritized differential diagnosis for intrusive terrifying thoughts of contamination leading to washing hands 50 times daily until skin bleeds
Distinguish OCD from psychosis, generalized anxiety, illness anxiety, trauma-related symptoms, and substance- or medication-induced presentations
Implement ERP and safe SSRI prescribing, monitoring, and emergency escalation

teaching.diagnosis: Obsessive-compulsive disorder, contamination obsessions with washing compulsions, severe
teaching.one_liner: Psychiatric evaluation for patient presenting with intrusive terrifying thoughts of contamination leading to washing hands 50 times daily until skin bleeds.
red_flags: Suicidal intent, self-harm, threats toward others, or inability to maintain nutrition, hydration, hygiene, or shelter
Fixed delusional beliefs, hallucinations, mania, confusion, fluctuating attention, intoxication, or withdrawal
Rapidly worsening or infected hand wounds, fever, or inability to stop harmful washing

must_ask.say: Can you describe the thoughts about germs or contamination that keep coming into your mind?
How many hours a day do you spend washing your hands or cleaning?
Do you recognize these thoughts are excessive, and how much distress do they cause you?
Have you avoided touching doorknobs, shaking hands, or certain places because of this?
Has the constant washing caused your skin to crack or bleed, or affected your daily functioning?

Have you had thoughts of harming yourself or anyone else, felt unable to care for yourself, or had experiences such as hearing voices, feeling unusually energized with little sleep, confusion, or recent alcohol or drug changes?

history.answer: I keep having terrifying thoughts that I am covered in dangerous germs, and I have to wash my hands over fifty times a day until they bleed.
I am terrified of catching severe infections like HIV or hepatitis from everyday dirt, door handles, and surfaces.
These fears began mildly about eight months ago, but over the last three months they became constant and completely out of control.
The dreadful feeling is there in the back of my mind all day, but it spikes into sheer panic the second I touch anything I think is dirty.
When I feel dirty, my heart races, I start shaking, and my chest feels tight, but it calms down after I finish scrubbing.
I refuse to use public bathrooms, I use my elbows to open doors, and I avoid shaking hands or hugging anyone.
No, speaking in front of people or being evaluated does not bother me at all.
My shoulders and neck are always tight, and I stay up late because I dread having to do my final cleaning rituals before bed.
I have to wash my hands in a exact pattern with scalding water and antibacterial soap, which takes me over five hours every day.
My skin is cracked open, bleeding, and stinging constantly because I wash so aggressively dozens of times each day.
Logically I realize touching a doorknob will not give me HIV, but the panic feels so real that I cannot stop myself.
I am falling behind at work because I spend hours trapped at the sink, and I haven't spent time with my friends in weeks.
Work has been busier with strict quarterly deadlines over the past two months, which made my anxiety much worse.
No, I have never experienced a traumatic event or assault, and I do not have nightmares or flashbacks.
I feel miserable and exhausted living like this, but I have never thought about ending my life or hurting myself on purpose.
No, I have never heard voices or seen things that were not there, and I know nobody is plotting against me.
No, my weight has been stable, and I do not feel sensitive to heat or sweat excessively.
No, I never get chest pressure or pass out when I walk or exercise.
I drink one small cup of regular coffee in the morning and no energy drinks.
I do not drink alcohol, and I have never taken sedatives, sleeping pills, or illegal drugs.
I try telling myself to wait ten minutes before washing, but the urge becomes unbearable and I always give in; I haven't had professional treatment yet.
I feel like I touched something contaminated with deadly viruses in a public restroom and I can't wash the germs away.
I'm terrified I'll pass a deadly virus to my family, and my boss is already threatening to fire me for spending hours at the sink.
I want a blood test to prove I haven't caught any deadly viruses, and something to quiet these unbearable thoughts.
I have high blood pressure and slightly elevated cholesterol levels.
I have never had surgery and have never been hospitalized.
I take lisinopril ten milligrams once a day every morning for my blood pressure; nothing else over the counter.
I have no known allergies to any medicines.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I work as an office accountant and live by myself in an apartment.
My mother has high blood pressure, and my maternal aunt has always had severe anxiety and cleaning rituals.
My last menstrual period began two weeks ago, my cycles are regular every four weeks, and there is no chance I am pregnant.
I am not currently dating or sexually active, and I have never had any high-risk sexual encounters.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 128/82 mmHg, heart rate is 76 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, temperature is 36.7 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
The patient appears anxious and tense, sitting upright and keeping her hands hovering above her lap to avoid touching surfaces in the room.

The patient is alert and fully oriented, with anxious affect, spontaneous speech, prominent contamination obsessions, fair to good insight acknowledging her fears are excessive, and no evidence of hallucinations or delusions.
The thyroid gland is normal in size, smooth, and non-tender, without palpable nodules or bruits, and there is no lid lag or exophthalmos.
No resting, postural, or intention tremor is observed in either outstretched hand.
Normal S1 and S2 with a regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs, gallops, or rubs heard.
Breath sounds are clear and equal bilaterally with no wheezing, rhonchi, or crackles.
Bilateral hands and wrists show marked diffuse erythema, rough scaling, and multiple dry fissures with raw excoriations on the dorsal surfaces, without purulent discharge or surrounding cellulitis.
